extracted.intended_audience: artists and writers (aspiring and practicing), readers interested in the relation of art, conduct, and religion
extracted.subtask_description: Practical and moral guidance for artists about temperament, conduct, imagination, and how life experience should inform artistic work. Advice applies broadly to writers, painters, poets, and other creative practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artistic life as self-development
rubrics_metrics.description: The artistic life is simply self-development; humility in the artist is his frank acceptance of all experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artist should accept all experiences (pleasure and suffering) as material for art and as modes of self-realisation. Example references: Pater, Marius the Epicurean. Anti-pattern: confining oneself to only comfortable experiences ('the sun-lit side of the garden').

rubrics_metrics.name: Art as symbol because man is a symbol
rubrics_metrics.description: Art is a symbol, because man is a symbol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every work of art converts an idea into an image; artists should seek symbolic incarnation of inner truths. Example: every moment of one's life is what one is going to be no less than what one has been.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humility = acceptance of all experiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Humility in the artist is acceptance of all experiences, just as love in the artist is the sense of beauty that reveals to the world its body and soul.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practically, this means not shunning suffering, disgrace, or sorrow but using them as material for growth. Anti-pattern: rebellion and refusal to accept privation, which 'closes up the channels of the soul.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Imaginative sympathy as the secret of creation
rubrics_metrics.description: An intense and flamelike imagination and imaginative sympathy are the sole secret of creation; the artist must realise imaginal sympathy with others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To create, the artist must understand and feel other people's conditions (leprosy, blindness, poverty). Example: Christ's imaginative sympathy is modelled as inspirational to artists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expression as the artist's only mode of conceiving life
rubrics_metrics.description: To the artist, expression is the only mode under which he can conceive life at all; what is dumb is dead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artists must turn ideas and inarticulate suffering into expressed images, words, or forms. Anti-pattern: leaving the voiceless unexpressed; failing to make 'the inarticulate' speak.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept both pleasure and suffering
rubrics_metrics.description: One should not regret living for pleasure if done fully, but one must also pass on to know the other half of life—the shadows: failure, disgrace, poverty, sorrow, despair, suffering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Art requires feeding on all aspects of life. Example: 'I threw the pearl of my soul into a cup of wine' but had to taste sorrow later. Anti-pattern: limiting oneself to pleasures alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebellion closes the channels of the soul
rubrics_metrics.description: A mood of rebellion closes up the channels of the soul and shuts out the airs of heaven; one who is in rebellion cannot receive grace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artists should avoid allowing prison (or any privation) to harden them into scornful rebellion; instead learn humility to remain receptive. Anti-pattern: adopting a front of brass and lip of scorn as a survival technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: The artist must be entirely and absolutely himself (individualism)
rubrics_metrics.description: He who would lead a Christ-like life must be entirely and absolutely himself; Christ is the most supreme of individualists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid living as 'other people'—do not let opinions, passions, or lives be mere mimicry or quotation. Possessing one’s soul (an act of one’s own) is rare and desirable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Love as the basis of imagination and moral life
rubrics_metrics.description: To Christ imagination was simply a form of love, and to him love was lord; the imagination is a manifestation of love.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artists must cultivate love (humility before love) as the root of imaginative power. Example: 'Love is a sacrament that should be taken kneeling.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Christ as archetype of the romantic artist
rubrics_metrics.description: Christ's life represents the ultimate romantic type—unity of personality with perfection, imaginative sympathy, pity and terror, and the poetic treatment of justice and mercy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artists may look to Christ's example for combining sorrow and beauty, imaginative empathy, and the elevation of individual experience into universal significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetical justice and sympathy over mechanical systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Christ's justice is all poetical justice; he had no patience with mechanical systems that treat people as things; for him there were exceptions rather than laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artistic morality should favour sympathy and particularity over rigid equal treatment; narrative or moral judgement in art can privilege poetic justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: The world must be made into images (idea → image)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every single work of art is the fulfilment of a prophecy: every work of art is the conversion of an idea into an image.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artists should focus on incarnation—making abstract ideas concrete and visible; this is the main task of art and the artist's vocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surrender to the moment; cultivate beautiful moments
rubrics_metrics.description: Those whom he saved from their sins are saved simply for beautiful moments in their lives; every moment should be beautiful and the soul should be ready for the coming of the bridegroom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artists should value and create 'beautiful moments'—rich sensory or moral instants. Anti-pattern: philistinism and preoccupation with dull respectability that miss such moments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philistinism as the chief enemy
rubrics_metrics.description: Philistinism—dull inaccessibility to ideas, dull respectability, tedious orthodoxy, worship of vulgar success—is the note of the age and the enemy of imagination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artists must actively oppose Philistinism (ridiculous estimate of worldly success, cold philanthropies, tedious formalisms). Example: Christ mocked the 'whited sepulchre' of respectability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repentance as initiation and means to alter the past
rubrics_metrics.description: The moment of repentance is the moment of initiation; it is the means by which one alters one's past and makes past sins into beautiful and holy moments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For artistic life, transformation of experience (including regret) into meaning is crucial; prison or suffering can help achieve this reinterpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: The artist should not adopt mere moral reform as primary aim
rubrics_metrics.description: The artist's primary desire is not to reform people or relieve suffering but to make beauty and to realise ideas; turning an interesting thief into a tedious honest man is not art's main goal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Art aims at revelation and incarnation more than social engineering. Anti-pattern: treating art as chiefly a vehicle for institutional moral reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study original sources to regain freshness; avoid stale repetition
rubrics_metrics.description: Endless repetition has spoiled for us the freshness and naive charm of the Gospels; returning to the Greek recovers verisimilitude and freshness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artists/writers should seek original texts or firsthand encounters with material to avoid secondhand dulness; repetition and over-familiarity are 'anti-spiritual.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity and childlikeness as artistic virtues
rubrics_metrics.description: When one comes in contact with the soul it makes one simple as a child; Christ held up children as types people should try to become.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artists should cultivate a childlike openness, fluidity and capacity for wonder; avoid excessive seriousness about material and the morrow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use imagination to reveal the voiceless and oppressed
rubrics_metrics.description: Christ made of himself the mouthpiece of the inarticulate; the artist should seek out those who are dumb under oppression and make their silence heard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artistic sympathy should reach marginalized voices; the artist acts as trumpet or medium for those without expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art should spring from within, not be made from without
rubrics_metrics.description: Romantic art springs from within through some spirit informing it; the dreary classical Renaissance made things 'from without and by dead rules.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artists should avoid adherence to external dead rules (formal prescriptions, slavish classicism) and instead trust inward spirit and imaginative urgency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagination as the basis of spiritual and material life
rubrics_metrics.description: In reading the Gospels one sees the continual assertion of the imagination as the basis of all spiritual and material life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat imagination as primary cognitive faculty: perception and value are formed in the brain; artists should cultivate imaginative faculties as foundational.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the transient eternal in art (sorrow + beauty united)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sorrow and beauty may be made one in meaning and manifestation; Christ's life unites pity and terror with sublime tragic effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artists should strive to fuse pathos and beauty so that tragic moments achieve a romantic, elevated art effect (e.g., Passion as poetic tragedy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Artistic temperament sympathises with what has found expression
rubrics_metrics.description: The sympathy of the artistic temperament is necessarily with what has found expression; behind words, colours, music or marble, the man and his message must have been revealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artists should pay attention to existing expressive forms as sources of empathy and artistic growth, while still transforming those sources into new expression.
